html:
SMTO-AUT-0016 — SMTO couldn't reach the Gateway securely to use this sign-in

GUID: 3e26f62a-8586-547c-8917-3d54b8042350
Slug: auth-private-egress-unavailable
Domain: AUT · Subsystem: auth-broker

What happened

  • This task needs to pass your saved sign-in details to the Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses to work on another computer) over a verified, encrypted link. SMTO couldn't confirm that link, so it kept them private and stopped.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways, find the Gateway this task uses, and select Check connection. SMTO only hands a sign-in to a Gateway it can reach and verify at that moment.
  2. Make sure that Gateway shows as connected with the Secure badge. If it shows Connection failed, check that its computer is switched on and connected to the network. Without a verified, encrypted link, SMTO refuses to send the sign-in rather than risk exposing it.
  3. If the Gateway shows Identity changed or Insecure legacy, ask the person who manages that Gateway to set up its secure connection again. These badges mean SMTO can't confirm it is talking to the same trusted Gateway, so it won't send private sign-in details there.
  4. Before running the task again, check whether its action, such as sending an email, already happened. Earlier steps of the task may already have run before SMTO stopped, so checking first avoids sending or changing something twice.

What success looks like

  • The Gateway shows the Secure badge and the task finishes without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it, with the Gateway's name, to the person who manages your Gateways. Don't paste passwords or sign-in codes into the conversation to work around this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The auth broker refused to release an OAuth credential because the selected Gateway has no verified encrypted transport (or its verified identity changed), or an unresolved auth_ref profile reached the Gateway HTTP client.

What this means

  • The broker cannot establish the required private Gateway route, or a raw auth_ref reaches a boundary that cannot resolve it privately. Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.

Why this can happen

  • The broker cannot establish the required private Gateway route, or a raw auth_ref reaches a boundary that cannot resolve it privately.

How to diagnose it

  • Check paired Gateway identity and encrypted transport readiness for the current connection; distinguish unresolved private references from ordinary HTTP data.

How to fix it

  • Check the target Gateway in Settings › Setup › Gateways: gateway_transport_ready requires a pinned TLS identity (tls_trust_state pinned) with an authorized controller, or an outbound wss session with a verified gateway identity, and that identity must not change during the consent wait (GatewayOAuthTransport). For HTTP profiles whose auth.type is auth_ref, the server broker must resolve the credential before dispatch; gateway_core execute_http_request fails closed on a raw auth_ref.
  • Select a paired Gateway with verified encrypted transport before executing the authorized consumer operation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the reported condition and check delivery evidence before starting another operation.

How to verify the fix

  • The authorized consumer receives its operation-bound credential only through the verified private route.

What not to do

  • Do not expose passwords, access tokens, authorization codes or SMTP authentication payloads.
  • Do not automatically repeat an operation whose remote effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
